'''''Coleostephus myconis''''', known as the '''corn marigold''', is an [[Annual plant|annual]] [[herbaceous]] plant belonging to the genus ''[[Coleostephus]]'' of the family [[Asteraceae]].

==Description==
''Coleostephus myconis'' is an annual plant that reaches a height of {{convert|20|-|50|cm|0}}.<ref name=UMA/><ref name=FE>Pignatti S. - Flora d'Italia (3 vol.) - Edagricole – 1982, Vol. III, p. 88</ref> It is glabrous to hairy, the stem is erect, usually branched.<ref name=UMA/> The lower leaves are spatulate.<ref name=UMA/> the median ones are lanceolate, dentate,<ref name=UMA/> more or less [[wikt:amplexicaul|amplexicaul]].<ref name=UMA/> [[Inflorescence]]s are orange-yellow, about {{convert|2|-|3|cm|1}} wide, solitary and terminal.<ref name=FE/> The flowering period extends from April to July.<ref name=FE/>

==Distribution and ecology==
''C. myconis'' occurs in the Mediterranean region of southern Europe. It usually grows in grassy fields, at altitudes of {{convert|0|-|800|m}}.<ref name=FE/> It has also been introduced in the south of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, where it is considered an invasive species.<ref name=UMA/><ref name=FE/><ref name=zip>[http://zipcodezoo.com/Plants/C/Coleostephus_myconis/ ''Coleostephus myconis'' at Zipcodezoo]</ref><ref name=wssa>[http://wssa.net/wp-content/uploads/Coleostephus-myconis.pdf ''Coleostephus myconis''] by [[Weed Science Society of America]]</ref>
